title: Lifestyle Inflation: 20 Ways Your Raise Disappears
description:
You got the raise. A year later your savings look exactly the same. In this video I go through 20 ways your raise disappears, from three angles: the money leaks (taxes, housing, cars, subscriptions), the psychology (the hedonic treadmill, new peers, status brands) and the long-term leaks, plus the 50/50 raise rule that lets you enjoy every raise and still get richer.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

1:28 How we got the numbers
2:13 Keeping up with the Joneses
3:12 Angle 1: The Numbers
3:20 1. Taxes take the first bite
4:42 2. The housing upgrade
5:41 3. The car upgrade
6:37 4. Subscriptions stack
7:37 5. Eating out more
8:28 6. Premium everything
9:24 7. Tech upgrades
11:01 Angle 2: The Psychology
11:08 8. The hedonic treadmill
12:04 9. A new peer group
12:53 10. Treat yourself, every week
13:39 11. Paying for convenience
14:34 12. Vacations escalate
15:19 13. Kids' lifestyle creep
16:10 14. Gifts and obligations
17:01 15. Status brands
17:56 Signs you're on the treadmill
18:37 A quick favor
18:52 Angle 3: The Playbook
18:58 16. Not raising your contributions
19:53 17. Higher limits, higher balances
20:50 18. Debt financed upgrades
21:43 19. No plan for bonuses
22:40 20. Locked in costs
23:33 The 50/50 raise rule
24:53 The same trap at three incomes
26:25 Undo lifestyle creep in 30 days
27:41 Two coworkers, same raises
29:26 Questions people ask
31:48 Recap: all 20 leaks
32:27 What to do next

Sources:
- U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Expenditure Survey (spending by income level)
- IRS, federal income tax brackets (marginal rates); Social Security and Medicare payroll taxes
- IRS and U.S. Department of Labor, 401(k) plan rules (employer match, automatic increase features)
- Thorstein Veblen, The Theory of the Leisure Class (1899): conspicuous consumption
- Research on hedonic adaptation and on buying time and well-being
- Raise, spending and growth figures: stated illustrative math
